title: A Tryouts for the Mixtape
premise: Rosalind Whitlock has survived two years at Ashgrove Academy by being forgettable, until a recipe card in his late grandmother's handwriting leads him to a hidden archive documenting the school's decades of quietly expelling—and erasing—students who knew too much. With the help of his only friend, Devi, he traces the pattern to a current trustee about to be honored at Founders' Day. When Rosalind goes public with the archive, Devi's scholarship is threatened and their friendship fractures under the pressure to stay silent. In the end, Rosalind testifies before an emergency board hearing, trading his own place at Ashgrove for the restoration of every erased student's name—including his grandmother's.
about_author: Petra Okafor is a former debate coach who writes stories about teenagers who refuse to be reasonable. She lives in Lagos and Chicago, depending on the season, and keeps her grandmother's recipe box on her desk as a reminder that every family archives something.

chapters.title: Cardamom and Ciphers
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Sorting his grandmother's belongings over winter break, Rosalind finds a recipe card whose 'ingredients' are coordinates and initials matching students listed as 'withdrawn' in old yearbooks. The emotional beat is quiet dread—the moment invisibility stops feeling like safety and starts feeling like complicity.

chapters.title: The Withdrawn
chapters.summary: Alternating Rosalind and Devi POV. The pair secretly cross-references the archive hidden behind the library's locked stacks, discovering the expulsions were cover-ups tied to a donor family still on the board. Devi urges caution; Rosalind can't let go. The beat is rising tension and the first crack of disagreement between friends.

chapters.title: Founders' Day
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. At the ceremony honoring trustee Edmund Hale, Rosalind slips the copied archive into the commemorative display—then watches Hale have it removed within the hour and Devi summoned to the dean's office. The beat is the climax: exposure, betrayal, and Rosalind realizing silence would have protected everyone but the truth.

chapters.title: What Grandma Left Rising
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, closing with Devi's. At the emergency board hearing, Rosalind testifies, surrendering his scholarship to demand every erased name be restored; Devi arrives mid-testimony to corroborate, mending what fear had broken. The beat is bittersweet resolution—justice outside the law costs Rosalind Ashgrove but returns him his grandmother, and himself.
